content: 1. For children up to 12 years of age, the recommended dosage is 10 mg/kg administered orally or intravenously every 8 hours. 2. For bronchiectasis in adults, the first-line treatment for methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) is flucloxacillin 500 mg taken orally four times daily for 14 days. 3. For methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) in adults: If the patient weighs less than 50 kg, the preferred regimen is rifampicin 450 mg orally once daily and trimethoprim 200 mg orally twice daily for 14 days. If the patient weighs more than 50 kg, the preferred regimen is rifampicin 600 mg orally once daily and trimethoprim 200 mg orally twice daily for 14 days. 4. For MRSA in adults, alternative regimens include: Vancomycin 1 g intravenously twice daily, with serum levels monitored and doses adjusted accordingly. Teicoplanin 400 mg once daily for 14 days. 5. For second-line treatment of MSSA in adults, clarithromycin 500 mg orally twice daily for 14 days is recommended. 6. For second-line treatment of MRSA in adults: If the patient weighs less than 50 kg, the preferred regimen is rifampicin 450 mg orally once daily and doxycycline 200 mg orally once daily for 14 days. If the patient weighs more than 50 kg, the preferred regimen is rifampicin 600 mg orally once daily and doxycycline 200 mg orally once daily for 14 days. Third-line treatment includes linezolid 600 mg orally twice daily for 14 days. 7. For children under 12 years of age with MRSA, the preferred regimen is trimethoprim 4–6 mg/kg/day orally every 12 hours. 8. For children over 12 years of age with MRSA: Preferred regimen 1: Trimethoprim 100–200 mg orally every 12 hours. Preferred regimen 2: Rifampicin 450 mg orally once daily (or 600 mg orally once daily). 9. For MRSA in children, alternative regimens include: Vancomycin 45–60 mg/kg/day intravenously every 8–12 hours. Teicoplanin 400 mg once daily for 14 days. 10. For long-term oral antibiotic treatment in adults with MSSA, flucloxacillin 500 mg orally twice daily is recommended as the first-line treatment. 11. For empyema caused by MSSA, the preferred regimens are: Nafcillin 2 g intravenously every 4 hours. Oxacillin 2 g intravenously every 4 hours. 12. For MRSA-related empyema, alternative regimens include: Vancomycin 1 g intravenously every 12 hours. Linezolid 600 mg orally twice daily. 13. For community-acquired pneumonia caused by MSSA, the preferred regimens are: Nafcillin 1000–2000 mg intravenously every 4 hours. Oxacillin 2 g intravenously every 4 hours. Flucloxacillin 250 mg intramuscularly or intravenously every 6 hours. 14. For MRSA-related community-acquired pneumonia, the preferred regimens are: Vancomycin 45–60 mg/kg/day every 8–12 hours (maximum dose: 2000 mg per dose) for 7–21 days. Linezolid 600 mg orally or intravenously every 12 hours for 10–14 days. 15. For olecranon or prepatellar bursitis caused by MSSA, the preferred regimens are: Nafcillin 2 g intravenously every 4 hours. Oxacillin 2 g intravenously every 4 hours. Dicloxacillin 500 mg orally four times daily. 16. For MRSA-related bursitis, the preferred regimens are: Vancomycin 1 g intravenously every 12 hours. Linezolid 600 mg orally once daily. 17. For septic arthritis in adults caused by MRSA, the preferred regimen is vancomycin 15–20 mg/kg intravenously every 8–12 hours. Alternative regimens include: Daptomycin 6 mg/kg intravenously every 24 hours. Linezolid 600 mg orally or intravenously every 12 hours. Clindamycin 600 mg orally or intravenously every 8 hours. 18. For septic arthritis in children caused by MRSA, the preferred regimens are: Vancomycin 15 mg/kg intravenously every 6 hours. Daptomycin 6–10 mg/kg intravenously every 24 hours. Linezolid 10 mg/kg orally or intravenously every 8 hours. Clindamycin 10–13 mg/kg orally or intravenously every 6–8 hours. 19. For prosthetic joint infections caused by MSSA, the preferred regimens are: Nafcillin 2 g intravenously every 4–6 hours. Oxacillin 2 g intravenously every 4–6 hours. 20. For prosthetic joint infections caused by MRSA, early-onset or acute hematogenous infections with a stable implant and short symptom duration (<3 weeks) treated with debridement, the preferred regimen is vancomycin and rifampin 600 mg orally once daily (or 300–450 mg orally twice daily) for 2 weeks. 21. For hematogenous osteomyelitis in adults caused by MRSA, the preferred regimen is vancomycin 1 g intravenously every 12 hours (or 1.5 g intravenously every 12 hours if the patient weighs over 100 kg). 22. For hematogenous osteomyelitis in children caused by MRSA, the preferred regimen is vancomycin 40 mg intravenously every 6–8 hours.
